conventions.convention: Real matrices; d ≥ 0, m,p ≥ 1, q ≥ 1; samples are indexed 0 ≤ k < q at times kh with h > 0. Outputs have no direct-feedthrough term. Errors are deterministic additive vectors.
M_k = CA^kB starts at k = 0; an impulse at sample zero gives output M_k v at sample k+1. A^0 = I_d, including d = 0.
The realization procedure uses exact-real rank, SVD and Moore–Penrose operations; it explicitly reports backend failure and makes no finite-bit computability, noisy rank-selection or stability claim.
State coordinates transform by x-hat = T inverse x; consequently A-hat = T inverse A T, B-hat = T inverse B, and C-hat = CT.
The observability injectivity equivalence includes d = 0; the least-singular-value sensitivity bound assumes d ≥ 1 and full column rank.

load_bearing.statement: States obey x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k and exact outputs obey y_k=Cx_k; Markov parameters are M_k:=CA^kB, with the stated finite real dimensions and zero-dimensional convention.

Given d ≥ 0, m,p,q ≥ 1 and exact M_0,…,M_{2q−1}, form H_0=[M_{i+j}] and H_1=[M_{i+j+1}]. Require rank H_0=d, construct full-rank factors H_0=O-hat R-hat, compute their Moore–Penrose inverses, and return A-hat=O-hat-plus H_1 R-hat-plus with the first input and output blocks as B-hat,C-hat; return the specified failure statuses when checks fail.

For every noiseless real discrete experiment and invertible T, the transformed matrices T inverse A T, T inverse B, CT and initial state T inverse x_0 give the same outputs for every common finite input sequence.

The corrected output stack is z=O_q x_0. Its initial-state map is injective if and only if rank O_q=d, including d=0. For d≥1 and full column rank, the minimum-norm least-squares estimate O_q-plus(z+e) has error at most the Euclidean norm of e divided by the least singular value of O_q.

For d≥0, m,p,q≥1 and M_k=CA^kB for 0≤k≤2q−1, assume rank O_q=rank R_q=d and every exact algorithm call completes and passes its stated checks. The algorithm returns success and a triple (T inverse A T,T inverse B,CT) for an invertible T, including the unique zero-dimensional realization.
